author: Lintuxer
tagline: Sign in with the admin e-mail you set — file explorer
description:
NextExplorer is a self-hosted file explorer: it shows every directory you
mount under /mnt as a volume, previews images, video, audio, PDFs and
code, edits text files in the browser, and hands out share links with
expiry. Local accounts come with the image, OIDC is optional. It is a
single container with no database service — /config holds the SQLite
database and settings, /cache holds thumbnails and can be thrown away.

**Install it through "Custom install", not the blue button.** Switch on
"Advanced (show more)" and edit the variables of the service `app`:

- `PUBLIC_URL` — this machine's address including the port. A wrong value
  lets the page load and breaks the login, which looks like a password
  problem and is not one.
- `AUTH_ADMIN_EMAIL` and `AUTH_ADMIN_PASSWORD` — the first administrator,
  created once on the first start. Both are public in this file.
- `SESSION_SECRET` — change it; sessions are signed with it.
- `PUID`/`PGID` decide who owns files the app creates on the host.

**After installing, open the tile and sign in** with the
`AUTH_ADMIN_EMAIL` and `AUTH_ADMIN_PASSWORD` you set — that account is
created once, on the first start. The shares you see inside are exactly
the folders mounted under /mnt; add or remove them in the same install
dialog, under the service's volumes.

tips.before_install: Set PUBLIC_URL to this machine's address including the port before installing — a wrong value lets the page load but breaks the login. Change SESSION_SECRET and the admin password as well. The mounts under /mnt are the shares you will see in the app; PUID/PGID decide who owns newly created files.
